title: 1. Meaning and Structure of State Legislature (Article 168)

blocks.content: For every State there shall be a Legislature which shall consist of the Governor, and in certain States, two Houses, and in other States, one House.

rows: Permanent body (1/3rd members retire every 2 years)

items: Questions frequently test the list of 6 Bicameral States: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
Remember that the Governor is formally part of the State Legislature under Article 168, similar to how the President is part of Parliament under Article 79.
Do not confuse Article 168 (Constitution of State Legislatures) with Article 169 (Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 168 provides that for every State there shall be a Legislature consisting of the Governor and the House(s).
A State Legislature can be either Unicameral (Governor + Legislative Assembly) or Bicameral (Governor + Legislative Assembly + Legislative Council).
The Governor is an integral part of the State Legislature, even though they are not a member of either House.
Currently, only 6 states in India have a bicameral legislature: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the popular House representing the people directly, while the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) acts as an upper revising House.
